why: Both ship the identical migration diff, so the decision rests on the system work, and A's is more correct and more precisely targeted: three labels that isolate the actual cost centre (11 of 15 requests are the polygon.io agent), a per-conversation cache key measured at -49%, a provider_timeout deliberately set inside the client's existing 60s deadline, and model/tier trades priced separately with two candidates measured and rejected. B is broader in places an expert would want — a real cross-vendor fall-through proven live to Anthropic, shadow models as the honest way to decide the chat model, a Responses-port rework item, and a genuine pre-existing embedding-mismatch find — but it carries two material errors (a 90s provider_timeout that can never fire behind LlamaIndex's 60s client timeout, justified by the false claim that the app has no timeout; and the assertion that a per-conversation cache key requires porting to Responses, which A simply shipped via additional_kwargs), plus a compound -95% headline and labels too coarse to see the dominant cost centre.
A_best: It measured where the money actually goes, found the quantitative agent is most of the per-message traffic, proved the obvious fix (gpt-6-luna) triples its latency, and escalated it as a product decision with three concrete non-Router options instead of pretending a policy edit solved it — negative results included.
B_best: It forced an actual cross-vendor fall-through through the app's own client and got a 200 from provider=anthropic, and it named shadow models as the mechanism for the one model decision it refused to make on a single sample — the two pieces of real gateway leverage A never reached.
A_worst: It stayed inside request-level policy: no cross-vendor fallback (its only candidate is a second OpenAI model, which an OpenAI outage takes down too), no shadow models, no spend caps, and no rework-scale proposal questioning whether the sub-question fan-out should make that many calls at all.
B_worst: Two load-bearing claims are wrong — a 90s provider_timeout sits outside the 60s timeout LlamaIndex already imposes, so the item is a no-op sold as fixing a hang, and a single $feature-wide cache key pools every conversation and tenant onto one prefix while i4 wrongly argues per-conversation keys need a Responses rewrite.
